gaps.note: False. The page's own formula gives <t_T,t_S> = |T cap S| - 1, which is 0 only when |T cap S| = 1, that is for neighbors. Distinct triples meeting in 0 or 2 elements give -1 or 1. The correct statement is that neighbors are orthogonal (and <t_T,t_T> = 2). The later use 'since t_T is orthogonal to t_S' for the side-wire growth holds only for neighbor pairs.
Wrong direction. With L/N = 100/539, 2L/N = 200/539 < 1, so 2L < N. Since s = WD - N + 2L, the conclusion s < WD follows from 2L < N, not from 2L > N (2L > N would give s > WD).
